title: An Iron-Free NdFeB Tile Array in Square-Helmholtz Configuration for Homogeneous 20–60 mT Static-Field Exposure of Seeds: Design, Tolerances and Dosimetry Protocol
content: Seed magnetopriming studies expose seeds to static magnetic fields of tens of millitesla, but their exposure systems rarely meet the dosimetric standards of bioelectromagnetics. Fields of 20–60 mT are hard to produce homogeneously with NdFeB magnets, whose surface fields exceed 400 mT, while resistive coils of the required size dissipate 0.2–1.6 kW. We present an iron-free, coil-free exposure system: two 8 × 8 arrays of NdFeB N42H tiles (20 × 20 × t mm, 25-mm pitch, 200-mm plates) facing each other across a gap. A thin magnetized plate is equivalent to a current loop around its edge, so the pair is a square Helmholtz arrangement whose optimum gap, 0.5445 W for thin plates, is shifted by finite thickness to 99–106 mm; operating just beyond it gives a computed relative standard deviation of 0.11% of Bz over a 50-mm seed disk at 20, 40 and 60 mT, set by tile thickness (4, 8 and 12 mm). The recoil permeability of the tiles reduces the field by 3–4%, the dense array drives the internal field to −890 kA/m, beyond the knee of grade N42, and a Monte Carlo tolerance analysis keeps the inhomogeneity below 0.6%. Forces, stray fields, cost, a sham-controlled dosimetry protocol and a single-device validation plan are given.
